questions.question:
Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.

The doctor is treating the patient.

options.text: The patient is treated by the doctor.
The patient is being treated by the doctor.
The patient is being treating by the doctor.
The patient has been treated by the doctor.

questions.solution:
The** correct **answer is** option 2)**

**__Rule__: Change of tense __does not take place__ with change of Voice form.**

Therefore, the passive form of the given sentence should also be in **Present Continuous Tense.**

__Formula for sentence in Present Continuous tense **(Active form**)__-

Subject + is/am/are + (1st form of verb+ing) + Object

__Formula for sentence in Present Continuous tense **(Passive form)**-__

Subject + is/am/are + (1st form of verb+ing) + (3rd form of verb) + Object

[the patient + is + being + treated + by the doctor]

(Remember that the Subject in Active voice becomes the Object in Passive voice, and vice-versa.)

Following this formula, we know that **option 2) is the correct answer.**

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill blank no 2.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__any__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• We usually use some with affirmative (positive) sentences and any with negatives and questions:
 
 
• She bought some tomatoes [positive sentence].
 
• She didn't buy any tomatoes [negative sentence].
 
• Did she buy any tomatoes [question]?
 
 
 
• However, there are some exceptions to this.
 
 
• **Any** can be used in a positive sentence to mean 'it's not important which one'. When we use any in this way, it's most often used with singular countable nouns:
 
 
• You can take any bus.
 
• Pass me any glass.
 
• Come over any Sunday.
 
 
 
• **Any** can also be used in positive sentences that have a negative feeling, for example if they include never, hardly, without:
 
 
• She never eats any fruit.
 
• We hardly watch any television.
 
• Julia left the house without any money.
 
 
 
• **Some** can be used in questions when we expect that the answer will be 'yes'. This is very common in offers and requests:
 
 
• Would you like some coffee?
 
• Do you want some sandwiches?
 
• Could you give me some help?
 
• Could you pass me some sugar?
 
 
 
 
 
• Here we don't know which interviewer we are talking about i.e. we are talking in general terms. So 'any' should be used here.

questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

The teacher says, "The Sun rises in the East.”

options.text: The teacher says that the Sun rises in the East.
The teacher said that the Sun rises in the East.
The teacher says that the Sun rose in the East.
The teacher told that the Sun rose in the East.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **O**ption 1 i.e The teacher says that the Sun rises in the East. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/dbd70ea3a020b879b11334d2851ddd8dbc9b8a39e2f5af5675278c35a1f54f8d.png] **Explanation **

To get the indirect speech we have to follow the given steps:

 
• We don't make changes in tenses of reported speech when reporting verb is in the present tense.
 
• When the reporting verb is in an assertive sentence we follow these steps-
 
 
• Reporting verb 'says'** **remains as it is.
 
• Connector 'that' is used in place of commas.
 
• The tense and personal pronouns of reported speech remain unchanged if it's a universal statement.
 
 

Hence following these steps we get the final sentence - *" The teacher says that the Sun rises in the East."*

Therefore we find that **Option 1 **is the correct answer.

questions.question:

questions.solution:

• Generally **no sooner** is followed by the conjunction **than**.
 
• When a sentence begins with adverbs such as “**no sooner**”, “**barely**”, “**hardly**” and “**scarcely**”, the subject the auxiliary are **inverted**.
 
• In the above sentence, we have already used the helping verb '**did'** in the inverted form so now there is **no need** to use the **past form** of the **main verb (ring)**. 

SO **option 1)** is the correct improvement of the underlined part. 

Correct Sentence: ***No sooner** *did the bell rang / **ring** ***than***__ the children ran out of the class.

It is clearly given in the second line of the paragraph that the movement started in **1951** from **Pochampalli, Telangana.**

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.

The children play on the park every evening
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option (1)**

 
• The phrase '**On the park**' is incorrect because a **park is a closed boundary **and children are surrounded by it so we use preposition** In** instead of preposition **On.**
 
• The preposition **'on'** is used when something is in contact with a surface in rest e.g. *The book is on the table*.
 
• So the correct sentence will be - "*The children play in the park every evening."*

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

Once in a blue moon
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option (2)**

When we say that something happens **once in a blue moon,** it means that it happens very** rarely or infrequently.**

**Ex -** *I read books once in a blue moon. ( I rarely read books.)*

So the correct mean of '**once in a blue moon**' is **rarely and infrequently.**

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

The boy said, "I am happy to receive the prize."

options.text: The boy said that he is happy to receive the prize
The boy said that he was happy receiving the prize
The boy said that he was happy to receive the prize
The boy said that he was happy to have received the prize

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option (3).**

 
• Reported speech of the given sentence is an assertive sentence.
 
• So now connector** that** will be used in place of commas.
 
• Reporting verb** said** is not followed by **to** so it won't be changed into** told.**
 
• Now tense(** Am into was**) and pronouns of reported speech(** I into he**) will change according to reporting verb part.
 
• **"*****The boy said that he was happy to receive the prize."** *is the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

questions.question:
Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence

My friend said, "Can I buy some sweets?"

options.text: My friend asked if he could buy some sweets.
My friend said that he wanted to buy some sweets.
My friend requested me to buy some sweets.
My friend said that he to buy some sweets

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **option (1)**.

 
• Reported speech of the given sentence is an** imperative sentence** which is a **request.**
 
• So the reporting verb** said** will be changed into **requested** and connector** 'if'** will be used.
 
• And rest of the sentence will follow** if** in **assertive form.**
 
• **'Can'** will become** 'could'** as per change into the **tense **and** 'I'** into** 'he'**.
 
• "* My friend asked if he could buy some sweets." *is the correct indirect form of the given sentence.

questions.question:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error.

I have been living in Delhi since many years.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option (1)**

 
• Prepositions **since and for** are used before the **period of time** in **perfect **and** perfect continuous tenses.**
 
• **Since** is used before a **certain period of time** like since Monday, since January, since 2018, etc.
 
• **For** is used before** an uncertain period of time** like for two days, for four months, for six years, etc.
 
• So here** for** will be used in place of **since.**

All students **__has a dream__ **to study in a good university.
questions.solution:

'All students' is a **plural subject** so it will take a plural verb. So helping verb '**have'** will be used in place of** 'has'**.

" *All the students have a dream to study in a good university." *will be an improved sentence.

questions.question:
**Select the alternative that will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case there is no improvement select “No improvement”.**

My friend said, “Can you please **__suggest for __**me** **a good school in the neighbourhood?”
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__suggest to__**

**__*Key Points__**

__
 
• We can use a noun phrase as the object of suggest*:

 **Example: ***Can you suggest a good restaurant in this part of town?*
 
• **If we need to mention the person who receives the suggestion,** we use a **to-construction:

 Example: ***My teacher **suggested an exam to me** which I could take at the end of the year.*
 
• Here, the person who received the suggestion is also mentioned so 'to-construction' will be used.

**The correct sentence is: ***My friend said, “Can you please **suggest to **me a good school in the neighbourhood?”*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__***

 
• When we suggest an action to someone, we can use a that-clause. 

 **Example:* ****I **suggest (that) **you leave here around four o’clock. The traffic gets very bad from about 4.30 onwards.*
 
• We can use suggest with the -ing form of a verb when we mention an action but do not mention the person who will do it, because it is understood in the context:

 **Example:* ****She **suggested travelling** together for safety, since the area was so dangerous.*
